main_body: Flat snow ground tile pattern: repeating light blue-white snow drifts with grey-green dark clumps (rocks/shrubs) across the whole patch, seen from above as a terrain surface
top_band: none (terrain texture; no standing object, columns alternate snow and dark clumps with no top/front structure)
evidence: Terrain ground patch, not a standing object. The 3/4 contract does not apply to a seamless ground texture; the column scan shows a repeating texture pattern of snow and dark clumps rather than any top/front structure. No side faces and no elevation drawing. Accepted as terrain.

style.evidence: Candidate has 8 distinct colours and a median of 8 per tile, compared with grass at 26 per tile and 80 colours, and paving at 7 per tile and 7 colours. It is on par with the paving reference and below the grass. There are no flat 5x5 fills (0%), and the dark pixels are tinted grey-green (0% neutral), not near-black. Snow shows about 5 lightness steps (white highlight, pale, light blue-grey, mid grey-green, dark green-grey) with dithered speckle in the dark clumps and a few bright sparkle pixels. Texture is present but the light snow areas are fairly smooth, and the pattern repeats regularly. Acceptable next to the paving reference, though less rich than the grass.
